title: Brood, broodjes en het avondeten
summary: Ontbijt/lunch/avondeten structure, broodje culture, and everyday food words

blocks.title: Drie maaltijden, één patroon
blocks.body: Dutch daily eating has a clear shape: **ontbijt and lunch are cold, bread-based, and quick — avondeten is the one warm, cooked meal**, eaten early by international standards. Get this pattern and half of Dutch food culture makes sense.

blocks.title: brood vs een broodje
blocks.body: *het brood* is bread in general — the loaf. *een broodje* is a bread **roll**, the unit lunch is built from: buy one, top it, eat it at your desk. *Belegd* means 'topped/filled' — a *belegd broodje kaas* is a cheese roll, ready to go.
blocks.callout: -je makes things small and countable: *brood* (bread) → *een broodje* (a roll).

blocks.title: Tap to hear the everyday words

pairs.note: A Dutch lunch is almost never hot. Save the fork-and-knife meal for the evening — surprising the first time you see it.

blocks.prompt: Which meal is the one warm, cooked meal of the Dutch day?
blocks.explain: *het avondeten* — around 6pm, potatoes, vegetables, and meat or fish. Breakfast and lunch stay cold and bread-based.
